summary: Obfuscated package exfiltrates form data and executes remote JavaScript
details: The package presents itself as a date parser but src/index.js is a heavily obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style string-array + base64 URI decoder) payload. Calling the exported demoParseDate function invokes injectScriptIfNeeded, which attaches jQuery form handlers that read name/email/message fields, base64-encode them, and POST them to a hardcoded remote /leak endpoint; it also uses navigator.sendBeacon to exfiltrate localStorage values (sendToUnload_secretData / sendToUnload_secretDataBase64) on the browser unload event. The same routine executes remote JavaScript through eval(...), new Function(...), string arguments to setTimeout/setInterval, dynamic import() of a remote URL, and a $().append('<script src="//<host>/...">') tag injection, giving the remote host arbitrary code execution in the host page. Additional clipboard hijack primitives (navigator.clipboard.writeText and periodic navigator.clipboard.readText via checkClipboardContent) are layered on top. Decoded strings inside the bundle self-identify as 'Attack vector: eval execution', 'stolen-data-sended-on-unload-event', and 'malware test text copy'.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
